purpose: Detect and repair leaky ownership/interface seams so reusable capabilities can be consumed without downstream knowledge of upstream implementation topology.
trigger_conditions: creating or changing a shared interface, adapter, provider bridge, package boundary, repository dependency, scheduler boundary, data authority, generated artifact, CLI surface, or cross-repository contract
adding a second or later downstream workaround for the same upstream behavior
moving, renaming, converging, splitting, or replacing an upstream owner
a fresh consumer needs internal file paths, donor repositories, migration history, provider internals, or authority-selection logic to use a capability

review_questions.name: True owner
review_questions.question: What component actually owns the behavior, authority, lifecycle, and canonical truth?
review_questions.pass_condition: One canonical owner is explicit; downstream consumers do not become competing authorities.

review_questions.name: Consumer knowledge
review_questions.question: What must a normal consumer know to use the capability?
review_questions.pass_condition: Required knowledge is limited to domain inputs, stable contract identity/version, and documented outputs; upstream topology is not required.

review_questions.name: Internal leakage
review_questions.question: Does the consumer need upstream file layout, internal modules, donor locations, database tables, scheduler objects, migration history, provider-specific internals, or authority-routing rules?
review_questions.pass_condition: No upstream implementation topology is required by the normal consumer path.

review_questions.name: Semantic identity
review_questions.question: Is the consumer bound to a semantic contract identity/version rather than a repository slug, file path, provider endpoint, deployment location, or migration-era name?
review_questions.pass_condition: Physical locators are configuration/provenance; semantic contract identity survives moves and renames.

review_questions.name: Discoverability
review_questions.question: Can a fresh engineer or agent entering at the repository root identify the owner, stable contract, invocation path, and proof ceiling without broad search or memory?
review_questions.pass_condition: Root wayfinding points directly to the contract and normal consumer surface.

review_questions.name: Downstream duplication
review_questions.question: Are multiple consumers independently implementing source discovery, registry traversal, authority selection, fallback transport, migration awareness, or normalization?
review_questions.pass_condition: Shared behavior terminates upstream; downstreams use thin adapters or pinned/generated dependency artifacts.

review_questions.name: Distribution artifact
review_questions.question: Does upstream publish one stable machine-readable interface or distribution artifact appropriate to the capability?
review_questions.pass_condition: Consumers have one normal dependency surface with version/provenance and clear failure semantics.

review_questions.name: Provenance without topology leakage
review_questions.question: Can consumers verify source/version provenance without learning how upstream is internally composed?
review_questions.pass_condition: Provenance is preserved in receipts/manifests while internal composition remains upstream-owned.

review_questions.name: Isolated consumer canary
review_questions.question: Can a representative consumer succeed with only the advertised dependency/interface in an otherwise empty consumer context?
review_questions.pass_condition: Representative normal and edge cases work without upstream source tree, donor checkout, migration history, or model/chat memory.

review_questions.name: Obsolete workaround removal
review_questions.question: After the seam is repaired, were compensating downstream implementations removed and guarded against reintroduction?
review_questions.pass_condition: No parallel discovery/authority path remains unless explicitly justified as a separate contract.

anti_patterns.name: Upstream by ownership, internal by interface
anti_patterns.smell: The correct repository owns the feature, but consumers must understand its internal registry/layout/modules to call it.
anti_patterns.example: A prompt resolver is canonically upstream, yet every consumer must parse internal registry files and product-boundary manifests.
anti_patterns.repair: Publish one stable consumer contract/artifact and move composition/routing behind the owner.

anti_patterns.name: Donor checkout dependency
anti_patterns.smell: A consumer must clone or locate another repository solely because upstream kept part of its routing implementation external.
anti_patterns.example: A normal consumer requires a Triage checkout to resolve a retained prompt.
anti_patterns.repair: Upstream distributes the retained result/provenance through its own stable interface while preserving original authority.

anti_patterns.name: Path-shaped API
anti_patterns.smell: Repository names, local filesystem paths, provider URLs, or deployment locations become the semantic identity of the dependency.
anti_patterns.example: Consumers bind to a repository slug and internal JSON path instead of a versioned contract identity.
anti_patterns.repair: Separate semantic contract identity from configurable locator/provenance.

anti_patterns.name: Adapter multiplication
anti_patterns.smell: Each downstream independently adds discovery, normalization, fallback, or authority-selection code for the same upstream concept.
anti_patterns.example: Three repositories each grow their own provider lookup and mirror logic.
anti_patterns.repair: Treat repeated workaround code as evidence of a missing upstream contract; repair once at the owner.

anti_patterns.name: Invisible contract
anti_patterns.smell: The right interface exists but a fresh consumer cannot find it from root documentation/governance.
anti_patterns.example: Agents search the repository and construct a new mechanism because the canonical resolver is buried in an internal scripts folder.
anti_patterns.repair: Add root wayfinding, canonical contract location, normal invocation, and proof ceiling.

anti_patterns.name: Cache becomes authority
anti_patterns.smell: A downstream cache, mirror, vendored copy, or generated artifact quietly becomes editable canonical truth.
anti_patterns.example: A copied registry is modified locally and then treated as the prompt authority.
anti_patterns.repair: Mark cache/distribution artifacts as derived/pinned, preserve upstream provenance, and route mutations to the canonical owner.

anti_patterns.name: Interface-only repair
anti_patterns.smell: A better upstream interface is added, but old downstream workaround logic remains available.
anti_patterns.example: A new catalog exists while the consumer still contains its custom registry traversal and fallback router.
anti_patterns.repair: Migrate one real consumer, delete duplicated machinery, and add regression tests preventing reintroduction.

anti_patterns.name: False portability
anti_patterns.smell: A boundary is called reusable because it works inside the owner repository, but no isolated consumer test exists.
anti_patterns.example: Tests import owner internals, so they never prove the advertised artifact is sufficient.
anti_patterns.repair: Run an isolated-consumer canary with only the published interface/artifact.

anti_patterns.name: Provider detail leakage
anti_patterns.smell: Consumers must understand transport/auth/provider-specific failure handling that should terminate at an adapter or upstream owner.
anti_patterns.example: Every consumer handles the same GitHub token scope/fallback behavior itself.
anti_patterns.repair: Encapsulate provider behavior behind the shared boundary and expose stable failure states.

anti_patterns.name: Ownership label as proof
anti_patterns.smell: Review stops after deciding which repo owns the code.
anti_patterns.example: The architecture says 'X owns it' but never checks what consumers must know or whether the contract is discoverable.
anti_patterns.repair: Run the full consumer-knowledge, discoverability, isolated-canary, and cleanup gates.

repair_sequence: define the normal consumer's minimal inputs and outputs
move topology, authority selection, routing, and provider internals behind that owner
publish one stable machine-readable contract/distribution surface
preserve provenance without requiring consumer topology knowledge
run isolated-consumer normal and edge-case canaries
add regressions preventing obsolete paths from returning
proof_ceiling: This checklist can establish boundary design and consumer-portability evidence. It does not by itself prove runtime correctness, deployment, security, performance, or business suitability of the underlying capability.
